topic: Power requirements, induced power, rotor, profile and parasite power and total power requirements.
syllabus_extract: Power requirements, induced power, rotor, profile and parasite power and total power requirements.
specific_objectives: 13.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the helicopter control, main rotor movements, translation flight, power, auto rotation, vibration checks and various adjustments.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of power requirement charts and identification of induced, profile, and parasite power components from IB diagrams.
intro_questions: What are the three main components of total power required for helicopter flight?
How does induced power change as airspeed increases?
Define profile power in the context of rotor aerodynamics.

development.content:
Definition of Total Power Requirements
Induced Power and Airspeed Relationship
Rotor Profile Power Characteristics
Parasite Power Components
Total Power Curve Analysis

Interaction of Power Components
Minimum Power Speed Analysis
Effect of Weight on Power
Effect of Density Altitude
Power Margins for Safety

Power Requirements in Translation
Comparison with Fixed Wing
Impact on Flight Envelope
Operational Implications
Review of Power Definitions

summary_questions: Explain how induced power varies during the transition from hover to forward flight.
Describe the relationship between parasite power and airspeed.
Why is understanding total power requirements critical for flight safety?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the power requirements of a helicopter in hover versus translation flight, referencing the concepts covered in LP 02 regarding basic flight mechanics.
